text:
sam: noticed a p99 jump on streaming chat after yesterday's kernel routing tweak. microbatch set to 2 for chat, 8 for completions. p50 ok, but p99 ~260ms -> used to be ~160ms. anyone seen this pattern?

maria: saw it in the dashboard 1hr after deploy. tail moves only during short bursts (traffic spikes). looks correlated with KV cache misses + kernel fallback to slower matmul path.

alex: quick profile: when mb=2 we often run very small matmul kernels that don't saturate GPU, plus extra kernel-switch overhead. for completions (mb=8) batching amortizes that.

kat: pasted the flame:
```
streaming_request -> choose_kernel() -> small_matmul() -> wait_for_kv_load -> fallback_kernel() -> write_chunk
```
notably `wait_for_kv_load` spikes for ~30ms on some traces.

perf-bot: trace uploaded: https://internal.redwood/traces/2253456789/traceA (contains p99 examples) :mag_right:

sam: is this primarily kv cache pressure (evictions) or our routing heuristic that picks a kernel based on instantaneous mb size?

maria: bit of both. eviction rate increases during bursts; routing uses last-known seq distribution and picks a kernel optimized for 1-2 seq len. when kv miss happens we pay both load + kernel setup.

alex: short-term mitigation idea: add a tiny hysteresis in kernel chooser: only switch kernel if new mb estimate persists > 150ms. avoids flip-flopping for microbursts. also try `mb_min=2, mb_target=4` for streaming so we coalesce slightly more.

kat: experiment CLI I ran (locally):
```json
{
  "streaming": { "microbatch": { "min": 2, "target": 4, "max": 8, "hysteresis_ms": 150 } }
}
```
results: p99 down ~40ms on my local replay for the spike traces. p50 unchanged.

sam: nice. what about cost/throughput tradeoffs? raising mb_target might increase latency slightly for single-turn fast chats. we need to keep SLO.

maria: measured client-visible latency: median unchanged, p95 improved slightly, p99 improved. throughput drops ~3% in steady state for that model because we hold a few ms to batch. unit cost impact minimal.

alex: kernel-wise, also cache kernel selection decisions per model+hw+seq-window for 1s to avoid re-evaluating for every request. lowers selector CPU and avoids short window oscillation.

oncall: if we change hysteresis, can we roll it to canary 5% on a spike-prone region? want to avoid global regression.

sam: yes. plan: 1) canary 5% region A with hysteresis=150ms + mb_target=4, 2) enable per-model selector caching 1s, 3) run replay suite with live traces for 6h and gather p50/p95/p99 + cost.

maria: I'll own the replay, alex will add selector cache, kat will push the config, sam please coordinate the canary.

kat: pushed PR: https://git.redwood/r/eng-runtime/PR-4312 (config, unit tests). includes metrics tags to separate canary traffic.

sam: perfect. please add an alert for p99 > 220ms in canary channel. perf-bot can subscribe.

perf-bot: alert subscription created for canary-2253456789 (threshold p99=220ms).

alex: one follow-up: if hysteresis + selector cache doesn't fix all tails, next step is prefetching small KV slices for active streams (cheap lookahead). that reduces `wait_for_kv_load` part.

maria: noted. will include a KV miss breakdown in the replay report.

sam: thanks all — will kick off canary in 10m and post updates. :thumbsup:
